Daruvar New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Daruvar, Croatia

Not demolished. One of the most notable Jews from Daruvar was David Frankfurter, son of a local rabbi, who in 1936 killed Wilhelm Gustloff, head of the Swiss branch of the Nazi Party — a significant act of Jewish resistance predating the war itself. During the Holocaust, Daruvar's Jews were attacked by Croatian nationalists and forced to pay a 'contribution' of 2 million dinars; more than 142 were killed by Germans and the Ustasha, and six Jewish partisans died fighting. This cemetery, built in 1862, was restored by local authorities in 1945, and a Holocaust memorial was erected in 1952; it has been on the official list of memorials for victims of Nazi terror since 1973, with further restoration in 1978. About 170 gravestones survive, inscribed in Hebrew, German, and Croatian, the oldest from 1868 and the most recent from 2015. The cemetery remains under the personal care of Zlatko Bienenfeld, head of the local Jewish community, who has described it as one of the best-preserved small Jewish cemeteries in the region.
